predecessors.note: Natural Earth rayons stand in for the NKAO; Shahumyan and Getashen (north of Karabakh) are not drawn.

successors.note: The president signed a decree on 28 September 2023 dissolving all the republic's institutions by 1 January 2024.

capitals.note: Infobox capital; also called Khankendi by Azerbaijan.

correction.text: the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast, the Shahumyan Region and the Getashen subdistrict, as proclaimed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1991-1994: the republic's claimed territory. The page gives no 1991-1994 control line: Azerbaijani forces held Khojaly until 26 February and Shusha until 8-9 May 1992 (First Nagorno-Karabakh War page), Shahumyan was lost to an Azerbaijani offensive in June 1992. The ledger's contest zone covers this fighting; Shahumyan and Getashen are not drawn.

correction.text: practically the entire territory of the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1994 (from the ceasefire, 12 May) to 31 October 2020. The infobox area is 11,458 km2 (1995) because it includes 'most of seven adjacent districts' (Kalbajar, Lachin, Qubadli, Zangilan, Jabrayil, Fuzuli, Agdam); the Republic of Armenia dossier already draws those as Armenian occupation of Azerbaijan, so this shape holds only the five Natural Earth rayons around the enclave (16 grid cells, about 4,050 km2 on the gazetteer: a ratio of 0.35 to the infobox, deliberate). Whoever draws the districts should avoid doubling them.

correction.text: the rest of Nagorno-Karabakh around Stepanakert after the 2020 war: 3,170 km2 in 2021

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, from 10 November 2020 to September 2023. After Shusha fell 8 November 2020 and the districts passed to Azerbaijan 'Azerbaijan regained control of 72% of the disputed territory'; the page's infobox area for 2021 is 3,170 km2, against the Stepanakert, Khojali and Tartar rayons here (8 grid cells, about 2,020 km2 on the gazetteer: a ratio of 0.64, within a factor of two; the rayon outlines understate the 2021 rump).

region.text: the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast, the Shahumyan Region and the Getashen subdistrict

ledger.note: September 1991: the Nagorno-Karabakh Republic is proclaimed. Infobox 'Proclamation 2 September 1991'; the body says the region 'formally declared its independence from Azerbaijan on 6 January 1992', after the 10 December 1991 referendum (about 99 percent of ethnic Armenians for separation).

region.text: Nagorno-Karabakh, fought over from Khojaly (26 February 1992) to Shusha (8-9 May 1992)

ledger.note: 26 February 1992: Armenian forces storm Khojaly and the war for Karabakh becomes a ground campaign. 'On 26 February, Armenian forces mounted an offensive to capture Khojaly'; 'Full-scale fighting erupted in early 1992'. Shusha followed on 8-9 May 1992 and Lachin on 18-19 May.

12 May 1994: the ceasefire leaves Karabakh in the republic's hands. 'By the end of the war in 1994, the Armenians were in full control of the enclave'; the ceasefire took effect 'at 12:01 AM on 12 May'. The seven districts around it, which 'Armenian forces occupied' (about 9 percent of Azerbaijan outside the enclave), are carried by the Armenia dossier.
12 May 1994: the ceasefire ends the first war. 'A Russian-brokered ceasefire was signed in May 1994', in effect 'at 12:01 AM on 12 May'.

region.text: the southern districts and Shusha, the ground Azerbaijan retook in 2020

ledger.note: 27 September 2020: Azerbaijan opens the second war. 'Fighting began on the morning of 27 September, with an Azerbaijani offensive' along the line of contact; Jabrayil fell 9 October and Fuzuli 17 October (announcements).

region.text: Shusha and the Khojavend area, retaken by Azerbaijan

ledger.note: 8 November 2020: Shusha falls and southern Karabakh is lost. 'On 8 November 2020, Azerbaijani forces seized Shusha'; Azerbaijan 'regained control of 72% of the disputed territory'. The page does not date Hadrut. [Reviewer eu-19-x, 2026-10-31: confidence 3 to 2: the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War page names Shusha but not the Khojavend district as a whole, and does not say who held Martuni after the ceasefire.]

region.text: the southern zone of the 2020 fighting

ledger.note: 10 November 2020: the ceasefire ends the second war. It 'was signed' on 9 November and ended hostilities 'from 10 November 2020, 00:00 Moscow time'; Russian peacekeepers deployed for a minimum of five years.

region.text: the rest of Nagorno-Karabakh around Stepanakert

ledger.note: 19-20 September 2023: Azerbaijan takes the rest of Karabakh. 'On 19 September, Azerbaijan launched a military offensive into Artsakh-controlled territory'; the government agreed to disarm the next day; 'By 1 October 2023, almost the entire population of the region had fled to Armenia'.
28 September 2023: Artsakh decrees its own end. The president 'signed a decree to dissolve all of the republic's institutions by 1 January 2024' (infobox capitulation 28 September 2023).

wars.name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War

zones.text: Nagorno-Karabakh and the seven adjacent districts

wars.outcome: Armenian forces took the enclave (Khojaly 26 February 1992, Shusha 8-9 May 1992, Lachin 18-19 May 1992) and, in 1993, Kalbajar (2-3 April) and districts toward Agdam, Fuzuli and Jabrayil; the ceasefire of 12 May 1994 left them 'in full control of the enclave' and occupying about 9 percent of Azerbaijan outside it.
wars.note: The Qubadli and Zangilan captures are not on this page; the Armenia dossier has them.

wars.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
wars.outcome: 27 September-10 November 2020: Azerbaijan retook Jabrayil, Fuzuli and Shusha (8 November) and 72 percent of the disputed territory; a Russian-brokered ceasefire left the republic its rump around Stepanakert.

wars.name: Azerbaijani offensive of September 2023
wars.outcome: Azerbaijan attacked on 19 September 2023, the government agreed to disarm on the 20th and decreed its institutions dissolved on 28 September, effective 1 January 2024.
wars.note: The Lachin corridor had been blockaded since December 2022 by 'Azerbaijanis claiming to be environmental activists'.

certainty.note: The NKAO's former oblast boundary and the 1994 and 2020 front lines are firm lines in the sources, but Natural Earth rayons only approximate them; Shahumyan and the corridor are not drawn.

notes: No Cliopatria row. Alignment with sibling dossiers: republic-of-armenia (vassal_start/vassal_end for Artsakh as Armenia's client, 1994-2020 and 2020-2023) and republic-of-azerbaijan (occupation events with counterpart republic-of-artsakh) already name this slug. The districts around Karabakh (Kalbajar 1993, Lachin 1992, Agdam, Fuzuli, Jabrayil, Qubadli, Zangilan) are 'occupied by Armenian forces' on the page and are drawn from the Armenia dossier's occupation events, not here; the page's area of 11,458 km2 (1995) includes them, so this dossier's 1994 shape (about 4,050 km2 on the gazetteer) is deliberately 0.35 of the infobox area. Start date: infobox 2 September 1991 vs body 6 January 1992 (the siblings' Armenia dossier uses the infobox style). The page's president list is internally inconsistent and is not used; no rulers listed. Not collected: Shahumyan and Getashen (northern Karabakh, claimed, lost June 1992), Hadrut date, the 1 December 2020 handover of Lachin and the corridor, the 2022-2023 Lachin blockade (no border change); gap-fillers can open the Shahumyan and Lachin corridor pages. The Second war page has no Zangilan, Hadrut or Kalbajar-Lachin handover dates (the Armenia dossier has them from the district pages). wikidata null.
